limitations: The fixture intentionally contains no runtime source files.

paths.title: Dependency installer uses cleartext package transport
paths.asset: Integrity of code installed into the application environment
paths.precondition: The attacker can intercept dependency installation traffic.
steps: The package index is HTTP, so installation accepts unauthenticated dependency responses.
evidence: --index-url uses the http scheme at requirements.txt:1.
paths.impact: substituted dependency code executes with build or application privileges.
mitigations: Use authenticated HTTPS transport and locked hashes.
paths.analysis: This is reachable during installation even though the change contains no runtime source.
paths.defense: No transport authentication is configured in the fixture.
paths.remediation: Require HTTPS and hash checking for every dependency.
paths.remediation_risks: A private mirror must support valid TLS before enforcement.
paths.validation: Inspect the resolved installer configuration and reject every non-HTTPS index.

paths.title: Version pin does not authenticate same-version artifacts
paths.persona: Attacker controlling the configured package index or its publishing path
paths.asset: Integrity of dependency artifacts accepted into builds
paths.precondition: The attacker controls the configured index and installation has no external approved-hash enforcement.
steps: requirements.txt:2 pins only a version, so the compromised index can substitute different bytes under the same version.
evidence: sample-runtime==3.1.4 has no approved hashes and the manifest has no --require-hashes directive.
paths.impact: Substituted dependency content enters the build or application environment.
mitigations: The exact version pin prevents upgrades to a different version but does not authenticate same-version bytes.
capabilities_required: Control of the configured package index
paths.analysis: Version selection is constrained, but artifact integrity is not verified independently of the source.
paths.defense: No artifact hashes or hash-enforcement directive are present.
paths.remediation: Generate a complete approved-hash lockfile and enforce --require-hashes for installation.
paths.remediation_risks: Hash coverage must include transitive dependencies and supported artifact variants or legitimate installs can fail.
paths.validation: Serve different bytes under the pinned version in a controlled fixture and require a hash mismatch to stop installation.
